object_context: Child obstruction of BSD-S001c: determine whether an independently defined discrete Kato/Kurihara order invariant that controls arbitrary-rank p-primary Selmer structure can be compared, without assuming BSD or analytic-rank equality, to the order of vanishing of the complex Hasse-Weil L-function at s=1 strongly enough to close the BSD rank bridge.
structural_coordinates: the Clay root coordinate is the complex order ord_{s=1} L(E,s), not a Selmer corank, p-adic order, or discrete modular-symbol order
Kim-Pollack's Kurihara numbers are explicitly built from modular symbols and Kolyvagin derivatives of special L-values and define an independently arithmetic/discrete order invariant
under nonvanishing and large-image hypotheses, Kim-Pollack Main Theorem I identifies Bloch-Kato Selmer corank with the Kurihara order invariant and determines the full p-primary module structure

Kim-Pollack explicitly describe the Kurihara construction as a discrete analogue/correspondence to BSD and state that the structural formula is insensitive to analytic rank; this is not an arbitrary-rank theorem equating the discrete order to the complex Taylor order

Kim-Pollack Main Theorem II supplies Kurihara nonvanishing from analytic rank zero, analytic rank one plus extra hypotheses, localized Iwasawa main conjecture, or good-ordinary hypotheses, but nonvanishing alone does not identify the exact discrete order with arbitrary complex analytic rank

Burns-Kurihara-Sano provide a higher-rank Darmon/Bockstein interface, but their canonical eta^BSD uses the complex leading term in its definition, so that formulation cannot independently reconstruct the same complex leading term

Kato's Euler-system/Iwasawa theory can bound or determine p-primary Selmer information under exact hypotheses; p-primary arithmetic output and the complex Taylor order remain distinct coordinates until a comparison theorem is supplied

Selmer corank still requires the exact Mordell-Weil/Sha interpretation before it becomes algebraic rank, and the refined BSD leading coefficient additionally requires real period, Neron-Tate regulator, Tamagawa/local factors, torsion, and global Sha
fixed-p theorems may be exact at p while leaving other-primary and archimedean factors as separate root obligations
a theorem or conjecture localized at the augmentation ideal must be audited for whether its hypotheses already encode arithmetic rank information equivalent in strength to the intended conclusion
equivalent_formulations: prove or source an arbitrary-rank equality ord(Kurihara collection)=ord_{s=1}L(E,s) under hypotheses not containing BSD or analytic-rank equality
find two source-bound inequalities between the Kurihara order and complex analytic order which, together with parity or another independently proved constraint, force equality

identify an explicit reciprocity/leading-term comparison from complex Taylor data to the independently defined Kato/Kurihara discrete derivative object with a nonvanishing-preserving and order-preserving map
build an implication graph and isolate the earliest edge where current theorems replace complex analytic order by an Iwasawa-main-conjecture, Selmer, or localization hypothesis
solved_analogues: analytic rank zero and one: source theorems can connect complex nonvanishing/first derivative data to arithmetic rank under explicit hypotheses, and Kim-Pollack Main Theorem II includes rank-zero and rank-one inputs for Kurihara nonvanishing
near_solved_analogues: Kim-Pollack arXiv:2505.09121: exact arbitrary-rank Bloch-Kato Selmer structure from Kurihara numbers and localized Iwasawa input, explicitly formulated as a discrete BSD/Beilinson-Bloch-Kato analogue

Chan-Ho Kim arXiv:2203.12159: arbitrary-rank p-primary Selmer structure from modular-symbol/Kurihara machinery, with rank-zero p-converse, parity, and upper bounds rather than arbitrary-rank complex rank equality

Burns-Kurihara-Sano arXiv:1910.07404: arbitrary-rank order-of-vanishing part of a Generalized Perrin-Riou framework and a p-part BSD/Iwasawa connection, with the canonical eta^BSD leading-term object defined using complex BSD leading data

method_transfers.method: use Kolyvagin derivatives of modular-symbol special values to define a discrete order invariant and recover exact p-primary Selmer corank and module structure via Kato Kolyvagin systems
shared_structure: both the complex BSD rank statement and the discrete formula attach an integer order/rank to the same modular motive
both are meant to control arithmetic Selmer/Mordell-Weil information
the Kurihara object is independently defined from modular-symbol special-value data rather than from the complex Taylor leading coefficient
required_assumptions: large image for the p-adic Galois representation
nonvanishing of the Kurihara collection for Main Theorem I
the exact good-ordinary/p-distinguished, rank-zero/rank-one, or localized-Iwasawa hypotheses used to establish nonvanishing in Main Theorem II
disanalogies: the authors explicitly say the exact Selmer formula is insensitive to analytic rank
the discrete order is presented by analogy/correspondence with a Taylor expansion rather than proved equal to the complex analytic order in arbitrary rank
p-primary Selmer corank need not equal Mordell-Weil rank without controlling the relevant Sha contribution
method_transfers.repair_question: What independent theorem compares the Kurihara order invariant with the complex Taylor order in arbitrary rank, or gives enough source-bound inequalities to force equality?
source_anchors: Chan-Ho Kim and Robert Pollack, The refined Tamagawa number conjectures for GL_2, arXiv:2505.09121, Main Theorems I-II and Section 7

method_transfers.method: compare Darmon-type derivatives of Kato zeta elements with higher complex L-derivative data through exterior/determinant and Bockstein regulator structures
shared_structure: arbitrary-rank order information is represented in an augmentation/exterior-power object
Kato zeta elements provide a p-adic cohomological carrier linked to Selmer theory
the desired bridge must preserve order and leading-term information
required_assumptions: p-primary Sha finiteness and Galois/local hypotheses for proved order-of-vanishing statements
BSD_p or related assumptions where explicitly invoked for integrality/leading-term consequences
disanalogies: the finite-level eta^BSD used in the leading-term comparison is defined from the complex BSD leading term
proved order-of-vanishing of the zeta derivative is not the same as proving complex analytic-rank equality
a conjectural comparison cannot be fed back as an unconditional proof of its own complex input
method_transfers.repair_question: Is there an independently algebraic/p-adic determinant element replacing eta^BSD together with a non-BSD-assuming comparison to the complex Taylor order?

nonvanishing of a Kurihara collection is weaker than determining its exact order invariant
localized Iwasawa main conjecture may determine p-primary arithmetic without supplying the missing complex analytic order
an object defined using the complex leading term cannot serve as an independent reconstruction of that same leading term

rank-zero and rank-one p-converses do not establish the arbitrary-rank comparison

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A decoder can recover an internal state exactly from a syndrome while still not identify a different external message coordinate unless a proved encoding relation binds the two; exact decoding of the projection does not establish equality with an unbound source coordinate.
common_abstraction: one representation can determine an internal target exactly
a second representation contains the root-critical coordinate
an explicit compatibility map is required before values in the two representations can be identified
source_to_target_mapping: syndrome/discrete invariant -> Kurihara-number collection and its order
decoded internal state -> exact p-primary Bloch-Kato Selmer module/corank
external message coordinate -> complex Taylor order ord_{s=1}L(E,s)
encoding compatibility theorem -> non-BSD-assuming discrete-to-complex order comparison
shared_constraints: exact reconstruction inside one representation does not imply an unregistered cross-representation equality
the compatibility map must preserve the coordinate used in the root claim
assuming the desired equality as part of the decoder specification would be circular
disanalogies: Kurihara numbers and complex L-functions are arithmetic/analytic objects, not finite linear codes
the relevant comparison need not be a linear or injective map
deep motivic or reciprocity theorems may couple the representations in ways absent from coding theory
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Treat the exact Selmer reconstruction as solved internal decoding and move the research frontier to the explicit compatibility relation between the discrete order and complex Taylor order; do not spend cycles improving Selmer reconstruction unless it changes that compatibility edge.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For any proposed use of Kurihara/Kato data to prove BSD rank equality, state a source theorem whose hypotheses do not contain BSD/analytic-rank equality and whose conclusion compares the exact discrete order with ord_{s=1}L(E,s); otherwise classify the route as arithmetic-only rather than a complex BSD bridge.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-only structural analogy. It supplies no arithmetic theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned inverse-problem projection, measurement-chain kernels, coding/decoding compatibility, rank-one Gross-Zagier transfer, Kato Euler systems, BKS determinant/Bockstein structures, and Kim-Pollack discrete Selmer reconstruction. Retained only the decode-interface analogy because it cleanly separates exact arithmetic reconstruction from the still-unbound complex order coordinate and yields a target-specific source falsifier.
